result.verdict: Approve with changes. The planning correction does make the whole-framework map the organizing unit: every API family and reader need has a row, the records example is labeled as one case, and the next slice has a stated reason (View/Region are the core of composition, have the largest gaps, and Application already has more coverage). What's left is mostly leftover example-first wording, overlapping stage names, repeated slice definitions, and one missing rule that the next slice depends on.
blockingIssues: The plan has no rule for what counts as supported public API. Both plan.md and coverage.md say that an export or visibility alone doesn't make something supported, and that ambiguous cases need an explicit decision. But nothing says how to decide: which of source export, `.d.ts` visibility, naming convention, v4 precedent, or test coverage wins. Without that rule, the View/Region member audit can't be repeated or checked, and 'supported members accounted for' can't be falsified. Add a short rule to coverage.md before the audit starts. This does not block merging the planning files.
risks: The slice's scope can grow without limit. 'Linked shared contracts sufficient to use them' pulls in Events, State, shared class utilities/extend, Renderer/DomApi and the View `behaviors` option, and Behavior has no page at all. State which shared contracts this slice fully authors, which it links while still partial, and how View refers to Behavior before Behavior's page exists.

Links will break while the compact reference is being replaced. Coverage rows, the quick start and the records lesson link to `docs/api.md#view`, `#regions` and `#state`. Moving contracts out of api.md will break those anchors unless the slice either keeps stub anchors that point to the new pages or updates every inbound link. The 76-link/13-anchor check gives no protection after that move.

CollectionView reuses the shared View behavior and child forwarding (`src/mixins/view.ts`, childViewEvents). If the View page states shared contracts without writing them once in a shared location, the CollectionView page will duplicate or contradict them. This is the plan's own maintainability failure.

The baseline is a dirty working tree with local destruction-cleanup changes. Anything verified against it can't be reproduced from the commit alone. Record a diff hash, or say which verification waits for those changes to be committed.

The per-slice report asks for all six quality checks, but a reference-only slice has no usability evidence and only limited architecture evidence. Unless those two are recorded as 'not run / N/A for this slice', people may read unchecked dimensions as passed.
The plan's usability dimension may pull a non-author reader trial into this slice. For a reference slice, author lookup checks should be enough to call it done.
incorrectAssumptions: The README's 'Historical Stage 1 verification', 'Stage 2 results' and `stage-3-package-results.md` share stage numbers with plan.md's new Stage 1 (inventory), Stage 2 (concepts) and Stage 3 (evaluation harness), but they mean different things. A reader will assume they're the same stages.

The claim that the records example no longer drives the plan doesn't fully hold in README.md. It still gives example-specific instructions ('Use `@mnjs/data` for the first example's observable state…', 'the new consumer feature needs its own architectural assessment'), and it lists records and historical artifacts ahead of the peer comparison and the plan. In peer-comparison.md, 'Evidence to collect for the first slice' is written in the present tense as though it still applies.

coverage.md defines Complete as requiring 'answered representative lookup questions', but then calls those questions 'author lookup checks until an independent reader actually performs them'. It isn't clear whether author checks alone can make a row Complete. The simplest choice is that they can, with an independent reader recorded separately under the usability check.

'Application lifecycle already has more coverage' is the only reason given for deferring Application. That's acceptable. The stronger reason is that View/Region are what every other class depends on for composition, and the plan should say so directly.
missingTests: Compile the View/Region TypeScript examples against the package's type declarations. The inventory says public type exports should be audited with their owning API, but the slice's completion checks don't mention types.
Check inbound anchors after api.md content moves. Every link from quick-start, records, setup, the llms.txt entry point and coverage rows into the moved sections should resolve.
Do a duplicate-contract check between api.md and the new class pages: grep each moved heading and confirm only one authoritative definition remains.
Run each reference code snippet, or record for each one which source test or probe backs it. Otherwise the 'executable-source divergence' check has nothing behind it for the new pages.

Add a lookup question that doesn't involve composing Views, such as the order of Region show/empty events when replacing a CollectionView. This shows the index works for class-to-class lookups, not only for View on its own.
simplifications: The next slice is defined in three places: plan.md Stage 1, plan.md 'Next milestone and follow-through', and coverage.md 'Next slice'. Keep the details only in coverage.md and have plan.md link to it.

Split the README's reading list into 'Current' (plan, coverage, peer comparison, docs index) and 'Historical evidence' (stage reports, first-slice decisions, the earlier review, the contract evidence files). Remove the duplicate plan and coverage links.
Rename the new plan stages (for example 'Phase A–E') or the old files so the numbers can't be confused. Alternatively, add one sentence explaining the mapping.

Mark peer-comparison.md's 'Evidence to collect for the first slice' and 'Candidate package follow-through' sections as historical records-lesson notes, or move them under the earlier-comparison heading.
Stages 3–5 of plan.md, the pilot material, can stay as they are. Don't expand them further in this work.
nextSteps: Add a public-API decision rule to coverage.md: the sources checked, the order they're weighed in, and the allowed outcomes (documented / internal / deprecated / needs-decision).
In the Next slice section, list each shared contract as either fully written in this slice or linked while partial. Decide how View refers to Behavior before Behavior's page exists.
Add an anchor-migration step and a TypeScript compile check to the slice's completion checks. Mark usability as 'not run' for this slice.
Clean up the README: take out the example-specific paragraph, split current from historical links, and resolve the stage-number overlap.

Consider expanding the View row to name `template`/`templateContext`, element options/`setElement`, `isRendered`/`isAttached`, entity/state event bindings and the `behaviors` option, so the member audit starts from a complete list of member groups.
Then begin the View/Region member audit.
